title: Puella Magi Madoka Magica: The Different Story
label: Quick read (from summaries)
premise: A three-volume side story centred on magical girl Mami Tomoe, whose warm nature sits badly with a solitary life where 'survival often takes precedence over kindness'. Her hoped-for partnership with fellow lone wolf Kyouko Sakura frays, and later Mami faces Sayaka's fall and her own guilt (Yen Press blurb via AniList and MU; ANN review of volume 3).
life_message: Kindness and choosing one's own ending matter, even in a world that rewards self-preservation.

content.note: Battles with witches, guns and spears; deaths of magical girls (AniList Guns, Tragedy; MU Brutality, Violence; ANN). Gore level not described (to verify).
Horror genre (AniList), Despair and Dark Fantasy (MU); ANN calls the ending 'pretty depressing'.
Mami decides to die alongside Sayaka and Kyouko tries to talk her out of it (ANN); MU Suicide/s, Mental Breakdown, Loneliness.
Self-sacrifice and despair shown as costly (ANN).
Spin-off of a large franchise; based on a drama CD (MU).

dominant: Selflessness versus self-preservation; despair and guilt; choosing one's own end

frames.concerns: Mami's resolve to die with Sayaka; despair without hope of redemption.

frames.aligns: Guilt and repentance over a selfish wish.

Tradition vs secular-rational.evidence: Religion tag (AniList) but no faith resolution reported.

Survival vs self-expression.evidence: 'Survival often takes precedence over kindness' (Yen Press blurb).

folkways.japan: Reworks the Japanese magical-girl genre, with its ideals of friendship and self-sacrifice, into tragedy.

delivery.evidence: ANN frames selfish versus selfless as 'interesting to explore', not heavy-handed.
delivery.note: The tension between kindness and survival is carried by the two girls' choices, per the blurb and the ANN review.

winners_losers: No one clearly wins; Mami's humanity is treated with sympathy while the magical-girl system grinds on (ANN).
